title: WALTEUR recipe contract
description: Portable, declarative, parameterized RUNNABLE workflow artifact. The interface lifted from goose's recipe system — NO goose runtime: walteur.js (the §5.7 orchestrator) is the sole interpreter. A recipe pins a reusable build/QA/ops flow as data (params + prompt + structured-output contract + opt-in MCP extensions + sub-recipe DAG) so it survives across sessions and operators. HONESTY: this schema is HARD on the recipe's SHAPE (a recipe.yaml that fails validation does not run); whether the recipe DOES THE RIGHT THING is PROTOCOL (judgment — the prompt + response contract are LLM-driven). graphify stays the ONE retrieval brain: any code/corpus lookup is a graphify EXTENSION, never a second index baked into a recipe.

version.description: recipe contract version, semver (e.g. '1.0.0'). Bump major on a breaking param/response change.

description.description: what the recipe does + when to reach for it

author.description: OPTIONAL provenance — who authored, free-text contact.

parameters.description: declared inputs. Each binds into prompt/instructions via {{ key }} at interpret time. required ⇒ must be supplied or the run aborts; user_prompt ⇒ walteur.js asks interactively; optional ⇒ default is used when absent.

key.description: binding name; referenced in the prompt as {{ key }}

type.description: value shape. file ⇒ a path whose CONTENT is inlined; select ⇒ one of options[]; date ⇒ a relative-or-ISO date string

requirement.description: required = abort if absent; optional = fall back to default; user_prompt = ask the operator at runtime

default.description: fallback when requirement=optional and the value is unsupplied. SHOULD be set when requirement=optional (enforced below).

description.description: what the param means + any constraint

options.description: the allowed values; REQUIRED when type=select, ignored otherwise

prompt.description: the per-run task message handed to the model, after {{ key }} params bind. Either prompt or instructions (or both) MUST be present — enforced below.

instructions.description: system-level standing directive for the run (persona, rules, the WALTEUR discipline to honor). Binds {{ key }} like prompt.

response.description: OPTIONAL structured-output contract. When present, the run MUST emit JSON validating against json_schema — turns a recipe into a typed function. Absence ⇒ free-form text output (PROTOCOL).

json_schema.description: a JSON Schema the model's final answer must satisfy (the response is machine-checkable, not vibes).

extensions.description: OPT-IN MCP wiring. The operator brings the infra ONLY if they opt in — standing-infra-in-the-repo is forbidden (anti-bloat). builtin = a tool walteur.js already ships; stdio = a local subprocess MCP server; remote = an HTTP/SSE MCP endpoint. graphify is the one retrieval brain — wire code/corpus retrieval as a graphify extension, never a second KG.

type.description: builtin = bundled tool; stdio = local subprocess server (needs cmd); remote = network endpoint (needs url)

timeout.description: seconds to wait for the extension to come up; absent ⇒ orchestrator default

required.description: false (default) ⇒ a missing/unreachable extension is a LOUD SKIP, not a hard block (detect-or-LOUD-SKIP). true ⇒ absence aborts the run (fail-closed; use only when the flow is meaningless without it).

settings.description: OPTIONAL run knobs. Absent fields fall back to the walteur.js / model defaults — do NOT hardcode a model id unless the recipe truly needs one.

model.description: model id override, e.g. 'claude-sonnet-4-6'. Omit to inherit the operator's default.

max_turns.description: hard cap on agent loop turns (runaway guard)

retry.description: retry policy for the run. Jitter is implied by the orchestrator — fixed-delay no-jitter retries are a resilience-lint R3 anti-pattern.

on_failure.description: abort = stop the run; continue = proceed past the failed step; prompt = ask the operator

checkpoint.description: OPTIONAL shell predicate that must succeed for an attempt to count as healthy (e.g. 'test -f dist/cli.js'); a self-validating checkpoint, not a sleep.

sub_recipes.description: composition: other recipe files this one invokes, forming a DAG. Each sub-recipe is itself a recipe.yaml validating against THIS schema. values pre-bind params for the child; sequential_when_repeated forces serial execution when the same sub-recipe runs more than once (ordering/idempotency guard).

path.description: repo-relative path to the child recipe.yaml (e.g. 'walteur-kit/recipes/run-tests.recipe.yaml')

values.description: param key→value bindings passed down to the child (overrides the child's defaults)

sequential_when_repeated.description: true ⇒ repeated invocations run strictly in sequence (no parallel fan-out); false ⇒ orchestrator may parallelize
